## Manchester Bathroom Leak: Practical Tenant Action Plan

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

You have a solid paper trail already. Because the leak has been unresolved for 18 days, the priority is to document the defect clearly, send one firm formal notice, and set a short but reasonable deadline.

## Repair Escalation Plan for the Next 7 Days

| Step | What to do | What to include | Target timing |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Create a repair log | Dates, times, leak location, damage, smell/mould, any worsening, who you contacted | Today |
| 2 | Organize evidence | Photos/videos with dates, copies of both emails, tenancy start date, rent receipts, any reply from landlord/agent | Today |
| 3 | Send a formal repair request | State the defect, health/safety impact, prior contact, and a clear deadline | Today |
| 4 | Follow up by another channel | Call or text the agent/landlord after sending the email, then confirm in writing | Within 24 hours |
| 5 | Escalate if ignored | Contact the council’s environmental health/private housing team and your local tenant advice service | After deadline passes |
| 6 | Keep paying rent | Stay current on rent and keep all payments traceable | Ongoing |

## What to Document Before You Escalate

- Date the leak first appeared and every time it worsened
- Exact location: bathroom ceiling, adjoining room, visible stains, drips, mould, soft plaster, peeling paint
- Any risk issues: electrical fittings nearby, damp smell, slippery floor, unusable bathroom area
- Photos and short videos showing the damage and the date taken
- Copies of both emails and any replies, including timestamps
- Proof that rent is paid on time
- A short note of any phone calls or in-person conversations
- Names of anyone who inspected, promised repairs, or attended

## Formal Repair Request: Tone and Timeline

Use a calm, factual tone. Ask for:
- Written confirmation that the repair is booked
- A specific inspection/repair date
- Temporary safety measures if needed
- A deadline for action

A reasonable timeline in this situation is:
- **24 hours** for acknowledgement
- **3 working days** for inspection or a booked repair date
- **7 days** for the repair plan to be underway, sooner if there is active water ingress, mould, or electrical risk

If the ceiling is actively leaking, sagging, or near electrics, treat it as urgent and say so clearly.

## Professional Message Template You Can Send

Subject: Urgent repair request: leaking bathroom ceiling at [your address]

Hello [Landlord/Agent Name],

I am writing to formally request urgent repairs at [address]. The bathroom ceiling has been leaking for 18 days, and I have already emailed twice with photos on [dates].

The issue is still unresolved and is causing ongoing damage. Please confirm in writing:
- when the property will be inspected
- when the repair will be completed
- what temporary steps will be taken in the meantime

As the tenancy began on 2025-11-01 and rent is up to date, I would appreciate prompt action. Please treat this as urgent and respond by [date/time, e.g. within 24 hours].

Kind regards,
[Your full name]
[Your address]
[Your phone number]

## Escalation Path While Staying Professional

- If there is no meaningful response by your deadline, send a final follow-up marked “urgent” and attach the earlier emails again
- Report the issue to Manchester City Council’s private housing/environmental health team if the landlord still does not act
- Contact a tenant advice service such as Shelter or Citizens Advice for help with next steps
- If the leak is worsening or affecting electrics, ask for an urgent inspection immediately
